name: TMP102 Temperature Sensor
description: The TMP102 temperature sensor allows you to use [Texas Instruments TMP102](https://www.ti.com/product/TMP102) and LM75 sensors with ESPHome. TMP102 breakout boards are available from [SparkFun](https://www.sparkfun.com/products/13314). The [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c/) must be configured first.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The I²C address. Defaults to `0x48`. TMP102 supports `0x48` through `0x4B`, selected by the ADD0 pin.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: How often ESPHome reads the sensor. Defaults to `60s`.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the sensor ID. Use this when another TMP102 platform must select one of multiple TMP102 sensors.

config_entries.label: Temperature High
config_entries.description:
**Required — set at least one of:** `temperature_high`, `temperature_low`.

High threshold number.

config_entries.label: Temperature Low
config_entries.description:
**Required — set at least one of:** `temperature_high`, `temperature_low`.

Low threshold number.

config_entries.label: Alert Polarity
config_entries.description: ALERT pin polarity, `active_low` or `active_high`. Defaults to `active_low`.

config_entries.label: Conversion Rate
config_entries.description: Chip conversion rate: `0.25Hz`, `1Hz`, `4Hz`, or `8Hz`. Defaults to `4Hz`. This is independent of `update_interval`.

config_entries.label: Extended Mode
config_entries.description: Use the 13-bit temperature format. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Fault Queue
config_entries.description: Consecutive fault conversions required before ALERT changes: `1`, `2`, `4`, or `6`. Defaults to `1`.

config_entries.label: One Shot Mode
config_entries.description: Keep the chip in shutdown between readings and trigger one conversion per update. The thresholds are then compared only once per `update_interval`, so ALERT can lag a crossing by up to `fault_queue` intervals, and `conversion_rate` has no effect. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Thermostat Mode
config_entries.description: How the ALERT pin behaves. In `comparator` mode ALERT asserts when the temperature reaches `temperature_high` and clears when it falls below `temperature_low`. In `interrupt` mode ALERT asserts on crossing either threshold and stays asserted until a register is read; because ESPHome reads the chip on every update, the pin clears at the next `update_interval` at the latest. Defaults to `comparator`.
